notes.title: Announcement on Completion of Ai Love & Adjustment of Its Operation Model
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]With the completion of the supporting free tutorial for the [i]Ai Love[/i] project – [i]Explanation of Common Functions in the Kirikiri KAG System[/i] – this project has now officially concluded in all aspects. We are delighted to share this joy with all of you.[/p][p]This tutorial systematically introduces the common functions of the Kirikiri engine based on the KAGEX2 system, and elaborates in detail on the implementation methods of basic functions for modern Galgame/AVG games. We welcome you all to watch it![/p][p]Video Collection Link: [/p][p][url="https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1y2eEzYER1"]www.bilibili.com/video/BV1y2eEzYER1[/url][/p][p]Ritsuai Works sincerely thanks everyone for your continuous support and companionship. Without your encouragement, it would have been difficult for us to successfully complete this project.[/p][p]However, we have to announce an operational adjustment here: One month after the release of this announcement, [i]Ai Love[/i] will switch from a free model to a paid model. The pricing will follow the minimum standards specified by each distribution platform, and the specific price shall be subject to the display on the platform corresponding to your region.[/p][p]When [i]Ai Love[/i] was initially established, it was positioned as an AVG project centered on technical exchange and entertainment experience. Our original idea was between commercialization and free openness: we hoped to maintain the openness of technical sharing – just as the Kirikiri engine itself is open-source – and advocate a healthy and open environment for technical exchange; at the same time, we also recognized that a completely free model would be difficult to support sustained operation and subsequent content development. To achieve a certain scale and quality of content, corresponding revenue support is indispensable.[/p][p]Even without considering the relatively large amount of program development work, we have also invested a lot of costs in material resources, dubbing, and music. The final effect has met expectations and even exceeded the passing standard recognized by the team. Although the team has always adhered to the original intention of technical exchange and did not take cost recovery and profit-making as the primary goals – even with zero revenue, the other incomes of Ritsuai Works and the personal funds of the main creators can still barely support the preliminary preparation of the next project – it is distressing that about half of the players have engaged in many invalid feedbacks or even malicious behaviors, including but not limited to blindly brushing achievements and abusing without reason. These behaviors not only fail to provide any constructive feedback for the project but also seriously violate our original intention of open sharing. Even some voice actors reported that their social media accounts were maliciously attacked – although this is an individual case, it is still regrettable.[/p][p]We can fully accept zero revenue from the project, but we cannot sit idly by and watch the community environment continue to deteriorate. Although we have repeatedly emphasized that [i]Ai Love[/i] is centered on technical exchange and entertainment experience, and have actively listened to players' opinions and respected their experience, the feedback we finally received is largely filled with meaningless content and malicious remarks, such as extreme views like "free games are not worth playing", "free games are just for brushing achievements", and "I only care about full achievements, and the game content doesn't matter".[/p][p]Game developers and players should have a interdependent relationship. Especially in the domestic environment where the Kirikiri solution is already niche, we have always valued and been willing to listen to the voices of every player. Since the game was launched, we have established a complete feedback platform, hoping to provide a channel for players to express their opinions freely. However, by the end of the project, the effective utilization rate of this platform was less than 20%, and it was also mixed with a lot of invalid or malicious content.[/p][p]This is by no means a healthy AVG game community environment. Even in the domestic niche doujin game community, after a work is released, it usually receives a lot of discussions and suggestions around the game itself. What makes us even more helpless is that many works with a lower degree of completion than [i]Ai Love[/i] have obtained more players who play seriously and valuable feedback because they adopt a paid model.[/p][p]This current situation has completely subverted our perception. We once thought that free openness would allow more people to experience the game, thereby gaining more feedback, supporting our large-scale content development, and accumulating experience for the next project. But the actual result is exactly the opposite.[/p][p]Therefore, we regret to decide: Before the official establishment and release of the next project, [i]Ai Love[/i] will switch from free to paid. All subsequent revenue generated by [i]Ai Love[/i] will be used for the development of Ritsuai Works' next project, in order to bring you more high-quality works.[/p][p]This is a difficult decision. We originally did not want to adjust the operation model, but the labor achievements of the team should not be ignored or even despised. Neither the rich system functions and high-quality music content recognized by major websites, nor the wonderful dubbing that covers almost the main storyline contributed by the voice actors, should end up like this.[/p][p]At the same time, in order to obtain sufficient revenue for the development of the next work, Ritsuai Works is now launching a program outsourcing plan, aiming to provide the project team with high-quality and low-cost AVG/Galgame program development and maintenance services. For details, please feel free to contact Ritsuai Works – Ritsuai Works Project.[/p][p]Ritsuai Works has always been a team and will continue to move forward as a team.[/p][p]Thank you all for your understanding and support.[/p][p]Ritsuai Works[/p][p]September 14, 2025[/p]

notes.title: 关于游戏的问题公告
notes.content:
[p][/p][p]Hello, fellow players!
[/p][p]This is my first time creating a game, so it’s inevitable that issues may arise.
[/p][p]Please contact me as soon as possible if you encounter any problems! Here are the ways to reach me:[/p][olist][*][p]Post a comment in the Steam Community for [i]Ai Love[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Join and message in the Steam Group for [i]Ai Love[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Send me a private message (PM) on Steam[/p][/*][*][p]Contact methods suitable for players in Mainland China: Two Bilibili accounts provided in the game’s README file[/p][/*][*][p]Discord Server: "Report error 4 Ai Love"[url="https://discord.gg/s44RCHFh"]https://discord.gg/s44RCHFh[/url][/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][p]Currently, some major critical issues have been fixed, and according to feedback from some players, the game is now playable normally![/p][p][/p][p]Due to my limited personal energy, some in-game content has not been fully translated. I apologize for this![/p][p]Here, I recommend a GitHub open-source translation tool that can instantly translate in-game text：[/p][p][url="https://github.com/HIllya51/LunaTranslator/"]HIllya51/LunaTranslator: 视觉小说翻译器，支持HOOK、OCR、剪贴板等。Visual Novel Translator, support HOOK / OCR / Clipboard[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Regarding future updates, I will no longer occupy public resources to issue announcements. From now on, updates will only focus on fixing bugs and improving game content.[/p][p]Thank you all for your support![/p]

notes.title: Content and Update Log for Ai Love Ver1.0 build.Hidesuwa
notes.content: [h1]Content and Update Log for Ai Love  [/h1][p][/p][h2]Version Description [/h2][p]Compared to the demo version, the official release version has seen significant improvements in both the content and quality.   [/p][p]This is the first official release version of Ai Love. I hope everyone will watch the video at [url="https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1DieuzEEDS"]www.bilibili.com/video/BV1DieuzEEDS[/url]. This video is intended to explain some of my thoughts on this game—I hope you can understand the mental journey I went through while developing it, as well as my perspectives on game creation.   [/p][p]Please note that this game was solely planned and overseen by me personally. My individual capacity is certainly not enough to polish the final product to absolute perfection, and [b]this has nothing to do with any staff or cast members[/b] (i.e., the production team and voice/performance talent). Therefore:   [/p][list][*][p]If you encounter any issues or problems, I hope you will contact me as soon as possible.   [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]If you find this game "just so-so" or feel it's not as good as \[xxx], I welcome you to give a thumbs-down—but I also wish that [b]you communicate politely[/b]. In that case, you are truly the ones who support my work.    [/p][/*][/list][p]Nevertheless, I still hope you will support and follow the staff and cast who participated in this game's production. Your support is the greatest motivation for them to continue their efforts!    [/p][p]Regarding feedback: I check messages regularly (though not on a fixed schedule) across the following channels:   [/p][list][*][p]Steam Community   [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]In-game feedback questionnaire   [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Contact information listed in the game documents (official Bilibili account and my personal Bilibili account)    [/p][/*][/list][p]Whether it's bug reports, suggestions, or casual chats, I will do my best to respond (and not with perfunctory replies like a simple "received").    [/p][p]Many people may not know that during the development of this game, I received extensive help from senior domestic players who use the krkr engine (commonly referred to as "Kirikiri"). Of course, they asked for no reward in return. However, I realized that due to the lack of relatively comprehensive tutorials explaining the KAG system (the scripting system for Kirikiri) in China, there is a significant gap in knowledge. This forced me to become a "jack-of-all-trades" who learned from various sources.[/p][p]Therefore, my next project will be Explanation of Common Functions of the KAG System, which aims to share the methods I've learned with everyone. I hope you will pay close attention to it：[/p][p][url="https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1y2eEzYER1"]www.bilibili.com/video/BV1y2eEzYER1[/url][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Update Log  [/h2][h3]Ver1.0 build.兵败如山倒desuwa  / Ver1.0 build.Hidesuwa  [/h3][olist][*][p]Added some in-game features.   [/p][/*][*][p]Fixed errors in certain parts of the game content.   [/p][/*][*][p]Integrated Steam platform detection functions and built-in game features; added the "Steam In-Game Settings" option within the game, and fixed bugs in the previously integrated functions.   [/p][/*][*][p]Added multi-language support. If you need to change the language, please go to the "Properties" menu of this game in your Steam library. Starting from this version, all language versions will maintain consistent update progress.      [/p][p]> Note: The built-in text display logic differs between languages. If you encounter text display issues (e.g., unreasonable line breaks) in a specific language version, please provide feedback as soon as possible. Thank you!   [/p][/*][*][p]Updated the game content to the official release version, revised the version number, and marked the version number in the appropriate location.[/p][/*][/olist][p][/p]

notes.title: A Letter to Everyone from Ai Love
notes.content: [p]# A Letter to Everyone from Ai Love[/p][p]Dear everyone,  [/p][p]This is 某刘某 from Ritsuai Works.  [/p][p]As you can see, this is a letter. First and foremost, I want to thank the Staff and Cast who participated in the game's development, everyone who helped me, and most of all, you—who are reading this right now.  [/p][p]This is 某刘某 from Ritsuai Works.[/p][p]As you can see, this is a letter. First and foremost, I want to thank the Staff and Cast who participated in the game's development, everyone who helped me, and most of all, you—who are reading this right now.[/p][p]Two years, over 700 days. That's the development cycle of this game, Ai Love, and also the time I've spent in the great place 淄博. And Ai Love is the "report card" I've worked on for these two years.  [/p][p]I hope this report card is "passable" in your eyes, the "grader" behind the screen. If you're willing to slow down and read this letter, and even install the game to play for a few minutes—whether you leave a positive or negative review—then for me, that's already a success.  [/p][p]Because I know this work has no real competitiveness in essence;  [/p][p]Because I know I've let down the expectations of many;  [/p][p]Because I know even though I'd essentially failed, there were still people waiting for this game to launch.  [/p][p]Countless times I wanted to give up, yet countless times I picked the project back up and kept going. And as you all know, the final outcome—this once "tattered and broken" project slowly took shape, became Ai Love, and finally landed in your hands.  [/p][p]So, thank you—thank you for clicking in and experiencing this game, even if you roughly guessed how it might turn out.  [/p][p]This game would not exist without those who still maintain the Kirikiri community in Mainland China. Whether it's D大, the author of the NVL Maker template used in this game, or the seniors who still keep the Kirikiri Bar community alive.  [/p][p]For a while, the Simplified Chinese community hasn't had a relatively complete krkr work in terms of programming—especially in the independent creation community. So when I received the notice that the game had passed review and could be launched, one of the seniors from Kirikiri Bar—who is also one of my mentors, 紫姐—jokingly said:  [/p][p]"国G黄埔军校最喜庆的一天。"  [/p][p]Even though Kirikiri is now facing a "gap between generations" (a shortage of new blood), the domestic krkr community is still supported by a group of reliable seniors—I consider myself very lucky.  [/p][p]So, thank you to these seniors—a large part of the in-game functions were created with their direct or indirect guidance. Without you, this game would never have come to be.  [/p][p]Thank you to Harmony Hall. I don't quite know what to say—all the music in this game is the output and legacy of Harmony Hall, as the studio disbanded at the end of 2022.  [/p][p]Fortunately, thanks to the studio's consistent high standards, we still obtained high-quality audio sources, including those that meet Hi-res standards. In the end, we produced *Ai Love Soundtrack* that meets high audio quality standards.  [/p][p]Moreover, even though the studio has been disbanded for two years, 乌拉—its long-term collaborative musician—still kindly took charge of writing the lyrics for the game's theme song as a favor.  [/p][p]So, thank you to Harmony Hall and 乌拉—without their efforts, this game would not have such competitive music.  [/p][p]This game will officially launch on August 25th, and this day also happens to be the birthday of Teacher 三七二十三, the voice actor for the character Wu Xiaohan in this game.  [/p][p]First of all, happy birthday to Teacher 三七二十三! Unfortunately, I don't have much to give you—finally, I used the computing power of my computer to generate a background image for you.  [/p][p]After all, all the voice actors for this work did this *out of passion* (for the love of the project). Every voice actor supported the game's production in their spare time. I feel truly sorry for taking up your spare time; what's more, due to my own lack of ability, I am fully aware that I failed to fully bring out the true capabilities of each teacher—and for that, I feel even more sorry…  [/p][p]So, thank you to all the voice actors for your generous support. It is your help that has enriched the content of this game!  [/p][p]Now, what is the point of this letter, after all?  [/p][p]That's right—it does not mean an end. Because I will keep moving forward.  [/p][p]Thank you to the Staff—I hope we can collaborate again in the future;  [/p][p]Thank you to the seniors who helped me—on my Kirikiri journey, I would not have been able to create a "passable" game without you;  [/p][p]Thank you to all the players—I hope you will continue to support Ritsuai Works, because I have long decided to devote all my energy to creating the next *real* work!  [/p][p]My philosophy for making games is simple: to let players open the game happily and close it happily. That's all there is to it.  [/p][p]I can't bear to see a system framework with enough functions "retire" like this—I haven't made enough of it yet! There are still so many jokes and gags I haven't put in!  [/p][p]Not a total defeat desuwa!  [/p][p]Finally, let me end with the lyrics from the game's theme song:  [/p][p]“风走过 天空才会泪流。”[/p][p]“爱上你 才敢毫无保留。”[/p][p]After all, I haven't admitted that I've failed yet.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45189990/6c89b6fcf13c27976ba674f0262f285463f79c7d.jpg"][/img][/p]
